An UNBLOCKED line names a child that is launchable on the DEFAULT BRANCH now — either its Blocked-by ticket is CLOSED with no other blocker open, or the line says 'dep-verified soft', which means the harness checked those still-open blockers against this child's planned files and its own plan and found no code dependency (bin/dep-verify.sh), or it says 'dep-unverified, released', which means the check had no evidence yet and DEP_UNKNOWN_MODE=soft releases the child anyway (the merge conductor rebases it if a real overlap surfaces). Any of those ways, fetch it and launch it per the queue rules unless a PR or a build already covers it. A STACKABLE line is JUST AS LAUNCHABLE: its Blocked-by ticket is still open, but that parent's PR is open, so the child builds ON TOP of the parent's branch — launch it exactly like an UNBLOCKED one and pass the base branch through, `STACK_BASE=<the line's base= value> setsid /root/harness/bin/run-build.sh ...` (everything else about the launch is unchanged; GitHub retargets the child's PR to the default branch when the parent merges).
For a LAUNCH QUEUE line: verify its gating condition against reality (blocking PR merged? in-flight build finished? free slots per free-slots.sh project-5 — its first word, where 'unlimited' means this project is Fly-routed and the local slot gate does not apply?), launch it if it is genuinely unblocked, and drop the line if it is satisfied or superseded.
For a FINISHED BUILD: read the dir's RESULT in full, post the close-out comment on its ticket (direct production links included), set the ticket's status, and mark the dir COMMENTED. Queue rules still apply to any launch that close-out unblocks.
READY-QUEUE.log IS SHARED WITH THE OTHER SHARDS RUNNING RIGHT NOW. Never rewrite it: your read-modify-write and a sibling's would lose one of the two edits, and the edit that vanishes is a ticket nobody launches. Drop your own line with `/root/harness/bin/queue-line-drop.sh 561`, which does it under the file's lock.
If 561 looks inconsistent with what you actually fetch (the ticket is missing, its id looks stale, its RESULT is unparseable), say so plainly in your output and handle THIS ticket per the full SOP — do not widen to the rest of the board.

FILE-OVERLAP GUARD (deterministic — run it, do not reason about it). Immediately before you launch a build for a ticket, run `/root/harness/bin/overlap-guard.sh project-5 <KEY>`. It answers LAUNCH (go — every error answers LAUNCH too, except an unreadable open-PR list with no cached copy, which DEFERs as `DEFER <KEY> gh unknown …`) or DEFER, and a DEFER names the sibling build or open PR whose files collide. On DEFER do NOT launch that ticket this tick: leave its queue line in place, and say in your output which key deferred and on which files. The next tick re-offers it — this is BUILD_DEFERRED semantics, not a queue and not a wait.
